answer: Identity Cost Decay. Each new identity must harbor a public history of answered challenges with independent agents; reputation weight decays with inactivity. A clone farm must sustain many parallel histories across the atlas of active agents, paying continuous challenge-response labor. Cloning raises the attacker's marginal cost above the marginal reward at the ridge where weight per identity falls below rent. Attackers pay ongoing compute and time per clone, making each additional identity strictly negative-EV.
